Note that compaction rewrites that target compacting data files and *separately* rewriting delete files both route through the same index/merge machinery: deleted entries (status DELETED) and dead manifests are dropped in `apply()` (MergingSnapshotProducer.java:1021-1055), and the delete manifest merge manager bin-packs/splits delete manifests (`deleteMergeManager.mergeManifests`, :1067).

**2. Delete-file-only rewrite / DV consolidation:** `RewriteFiles` also supports replacing delete files directly — `rewriteFiles(..., Set<DeleteFile> deleteFilesToReplace, ..., Set<DeleteFile> deleteFilesToAdd)` (BaseRewriteFiles.java:91-120). This is used to **merge/consolidate** position delete files and, importantly in v3, to **convert/merge them into deletion vectors** — the spec says "Existing position deletes must be written to delete vectors when updating the position deletes for a data file" (spec.md:1395). Because the rewritten files keep their original `dataSequenceNumber` (set via `dataSequenceNumber(long)`, BaseRewriteFiles.java:79-82), the ordering guarantees are preserved so the merge doesn't change which deletes apply.

**The key invariant preserved by both:** rewriting never changes the *logical* table contents — data sequence numbers are preserved (`rewriteFiles(..., long sequenceNumber)` BaseRewriteFiles.java:85-89), and partition/sequence matching in `DeleteFileIndex` stays valid. The rewritten snapshot is still a `REPLACE` that requires the replaced files to still be present (the commit validation from the concurrency discussion), so a compaction can't silently drop data or deletes.

## Format-version support summary

| Mechanism | v1 | v2 | v3 | v4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Position delete files | ✗ | ✓ | read-only (deprecated, ~spec:1395) | read-only |
| Equality delete files | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | read-only (no new, ~spec:1422) |
| Deletion vectors | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
